question: A person travels a distance of 25 km at a speed of 75 km/hr and then comes back at twice the speed. How many minutes did he take in total?
explanation:
Time for the first leg (going)

Distance covered = 25 km
Speed = 75 km/hr
We can use the formula: Time = Distance / Speed

Time (going) = 25 km / 75 km/hr = 1/3 hours

Convert hours to minutes

Time (going) in minutes = 1/3 hours * 60 minutes/hour = 20 minutes

Time for the second leg (returning)

Distance covered = 25 km (same distance as going)
Speed = Twice the speed while going = 75 km/hr * 2 = 150 km/hr
Time (returning) = 25 km / 150 km/hr = 1/6 hours

Convert hours to minutes

Time (returning) in minutes = 1/6 hours * 60 minutes/hour = 10 minutes

Total Time

Total time = Time (going) + Time (returning)

Total time = 20 minutes + 10 minutes = 30 minutes
